title: Credentials and What They're Worth
description: Understand which certifications actually matter for an AI-oversight coding role, what they cost in money and study time, and what they don't get you — so a certification decision is made with real numbers instead of marketing copy.

title: Proving You Can Do It
description: Build evidence of applied review skill that survives having no prior clinical employment — a portfolio of de-identified work samples, an audit write-up, and an honest way of explaining an employment gap.

title: Interviews and Coding Tests
description: Handle the coding test and the judgement questions that decide these hires — talking through a review out loud, answering escalation and disagreement questions honestly, and asking about volume targets before accepting an offer.

title: Accommodation and Disclosure
description: Decide what to disclose, when, and how to ask for what you need without over-explaining — including what you are and aren't required to say, which accommodations actually help this specific job, and when an employer's answer is telling you to leave.

title: Staying Current in Clinical Coding
description: Keep up with the annual code-set update cycle, guideline changes, and AI-pipeline changes at your own employer on a small, sustainable time budget — the final skill that keeps this whole track's credential relevant after the course ends.
